header.title: Open Pile Plan Studio
header.heroAlt: Open Pile Plan Studio: pile plan of an example distribution centre with coloured areas per tip level and, on the right, the pile options of the selected column
header.label: Foundations
header.tagline: From loads and CPTs to a well-founded pile plan
header.desc: Import the load points, CPTs and foundation advice and see for each location which pile fits, what it costs and how heavily it is loaded. Assign choices, let the app find the cheapest coherent variant and export the plan to Excel.

meta.description: Free, open-source app for pile plans: load points, CPTs and foundation advice together in one plan, with pile options, utilisation, costs and optimisation. In the browser and for Windows.
meta.title: Open Pile Plan Studio — OpenAEC Foundation

cpt.alt: Selected column with lines to four CPTs on the drawing and, on the right, a table with quadrant, CPT, distance and bearing capacity
cpt.title: See which CPTs govern a pile
cpt.desc: For each load point the app selects the CPTs per quadrant or within a maximum angle, with the distance and bearing capacity alongside. Lines on the drawing show which CPTs count; override the choice when you want something else.

optim.alt: Optimisation panel with the result: weighted neighbour differences, actual cost and the number of optimised locations, next to the new pile plan
optim.title: Let the app find the cheapest coherent plan
optim.desc: The optimiser looks for the lowest cost within your limits on the number of pile sizes and tip levels. It then makes the plan calmer: fewer differences between neighbours, within a small cost budget. You can see whether the result is proven optimal.

cap.alt: Pile-cap proposal of four piles under a column of the lift core, with the pile options and total cost per proposal
cap.title: Try more piles under one cap
cap.desc: Set a pile-cap proposal of 1 to 20 piles for a location or group and immediately see which pile options fit and what they cost. The proposal is stored with the pile plan; an overview lists all changes in the plan.

export.alt: Export screen with the pile plan's column settings and a table preview with location, coordinates, load, pile size, tip level and CPTs
export.title: A pile schedule the way you want it
export.desc: Choose which pile plan to export, which columns it contains, in what order and what they are called. You see the table straight away in a preview and save it as Excel or CSV. A change table compares it with an earlier version.

data.alt: Load point table: ID, X, Y and FEd per location, with the pile options of the selected location on the right
data.title: Your own tables as the starting point
data.desc: Import load points, CPTs and foundation advice from CSV or Excel, also directly from an RFEM export. Each source is kept as a table in the project. When the structural model changes, refresh the source: linked choices move to the new locations.

notice.text: Public alpha: the results support your design, but always have them checked by a qualified professional.

features.label: Features
features.heading: Everything for the pile plan, on one drawing
features.sub: Start with the highlights, or pick a topic.

options.title: Pile options per location
options.desc: For each location every combination of pile size and tip level: valid, insufficient or without advice, with the governing CPT.

compare.title: Utilisation and cost
compare.desc: Compare utilisation, bearing capacity and estimated cost before you choose a pile. Sort and filter every column.

multi.title: One choice for many locations
multi.desc: Select by clicking, with Shift or with a lasso; the table then shows the options that apply to all locations.

groups.title: Groups
groups.desc: Bundle locations into a group with the same pile. Groups with conflicting choices turn red.

cap.title: Pile-cap proposals
cap.desc: Try 1 to 20 piles under a cap, with indicative options and costs. Resetting everything takes one step.

lock.title: Lock choices
lock.desc: Lock fixed choices per pile plan; the optimiser then leaves them as they are.

legend.title: Legend and display
legend.desc: Filter by pile size and tip level, adjust symbols and colours and choose which columns you see.

cptauto.title: Select CPTs automatically
cptauto.desc: Per quadrant or within a maximum angle, with a distance limit.

cptmanual.title: Override manually
cptmanual.desc: Change the CPTs for one location or a whole selection at once, and restore the automatic choice whenever you like.

advice.title: Combine foundation advice
advice.desc: Several advice files and worksheets in one project, also as a table with one column per pile size. Conflicting values are reported.

optim.title: Lowest cost
optim.desc: The optimiser finds the cheapest assignment within limits on the number of pile sizes, tip levels and configurations.

coherence.title: A calmer plan
coherence.desc: Fewer differences in tip level and pile size between neighbours, within a cost budget (5% extra by default).

quick.title: Quick improve
quick.desc: A quick local improvement as an alternative to the full calculation. You always see whether a result is proven optimal.

variants.title: Several pile plans
variants.desc: Keep variants side by side in one project, with the total cost per plan.

import.title: CSV, Excel and RFEM
import.desc: Give each file a role before importing. An RFEM export is recognised; you first see a preview with any errors.

refresh.title: Refresh sources
refresh.desc: New loads from the structural model? Link old and new locations on a large drawing; choices and locks move along.

importplan.title: Import an existing pile plan
importplan.desc: An Excel or CSV table becomes a new pile plan, matched by ID or coordinate, with a check beforehand.

export.title: Pile schedule to Excel or CSV
export.desc: Your own columns, order and headers, pile numbering and units, with a live preview.

change.title: Change table
change.desc: Compare with an earlier pile schedule: moved, other size, other level, added or removed, with codes you choose yourself.

ifcpp.title: Everything in one project file
ifcpp.desc: Sources, settings, choices and variants in one IFCPP file, with undo and recovery after a browser crash.

mcp.title: AI assistant (Windows)
mcp.desc: Connect ChatGPT Desktop or Claude Desktop to the open project. Reading and editing are switched on separately.

download.browserNote: Rather not install anything? The app also runs in the browser.
download.label: Download
download.mobileNote: Open Pile Plan Studio is made for a large screen. Open it on your computer, or try it here in the browser.

columns.title: Columns of your choice
columns.desc: Choose, drag and rename the export columns, and pick which plan to export without switching the active plan.

marks.title: Pile numbering
marks.desc: Number piles spatially and give tip levels a letter or number code, from high to low or the other way round.

change.title: Change table
change.desc: Compare an earlier pile schedule from CSV or Excel with the new plan; existing pile numbers are kept.

codes.title: Change codes
codes.desc: A column with M, S, L, A and R for moved, size, level, added and removed; you set the codes and threshold yourself.

review.title: Link locations on a large drawing
review.desc: Start with the open cases, pick the old partner on the drawing and move on to the next automatically; the rest in one go by distance.

whatsnew.label: New in v2026.44.3
whatsnew.title: Custom pile schedules and change tables
whatsnew.desc: This release makes the export configurable, adds change tables and gives linking old and new locations its own large workspace.

files.a: Load points, CPTs and foundation advice as CSV or Excel (XLSX), loads also as an Excel export from RFEM. Also projects in IFCPP and existing pile schedules from Excel or CSV.

install.q: Do I need to install anything?
install.a: No. The web version opens straight away with a sample project. You only need the Windows app for the AI assistant connection and to open IFCPP files from Explorer.

cost.a: Nothing. Open Pile Plan Studio is free and open source under the LGPL-3.0 licence, without an account.

format.q: In which file format is my work saved?
format.a: In an IFCPP file: an open, readable project format with all sources, settings, choices and variants. You export pile schedules to Excel or CSV.

systems.q: Which systems does it run on?
systems.a: In any modern browser, so also on macOS and Linux, and as an app for Windows (64-bit). Installers for macOS and Linux are not available yet.

practice.q: Does it fit everyday engineering practice?
practice.a: Yes. You work with the design values you already have: FEd from the structural model and Rc;net;d per CPT, pile size and tip level from the foundation advice. Pile costs per m³ are set per project.

ai.q: What can an AI assistant do with it?
ai.a: The Windows app can share the open project over MCP with, for example, ChatGPT Desktop or Claude Desktop. The assistant can inspect data, compare plans and run the optimiser; editing is switched on separately. The web version has no MCP.

capacity.q: Does the app calculate the bearing capacity itself?
capacity.a: No, not yet. The bearing capacity per CPT comes from the geotechnical consultant's foundation advice; the app selects, compares and optimises on that basis.

optimal.q: Is the optimiser's result always the best?
optimal.a: Not always, and you can see that. The result reports whether the optimum is proven; with Quick improve or an interrupted run you get the best solution found.

try.q: Can I try it first without my own data?
try.a: Yes. The web version opens with a complete sample project, so you can explore the workflow straight away.

react.title: React and TypeScript
react.desc: The interface with drawing, tables and ribbon, the same in browser and desktop.

tauri.desc: A small, signed Windows app with the core running natively in Rust.

highs.desc: Open-source solver for the integer optimisation, in browser and desktop.

mcp.desc: Local connection for AI assistants in the Windows app; changes go through the same checks and history.
